Package org.geysermc.paletter.vanilla

Class BedrockItemType

java.lang.Object
org.geysermc.paletter.vanilla.BedrockItemType
All Implemented Interfaces:
ItemKey
public final class BedrockItemType extends Object implements ItemKey
A Bedrock item type. Vanilla types are the constants of BedrockItems; a CustomItem (and the item of a CustomBlock) has one too, so both are used alike: 

 ItemData apple = palette.item(BedrockItems.APPLE).toItemData().count(3).build();
 ItemData potion = palette.item(BedrockItems.POTION.variant(5)).toItemData().build();
A type is an ItemKey for its base variant, so it can be passed to the methods that take a variant. Items whose variants differ by damage (potions, banners, goat horns, ...) expose them with variant(int). The potions, tipped arrows, beds and banners have constants for them in BedrockItemVariants.

Equality: equals always works, and types are map keys. == works too for vanilla types, which are singletons (the constants), for their base variant and for registered custom content: a CustomItem owns its type (a CustomBlock its item type), and a palette it is registered in hands back exactly that type. Custom types made for an identifier that is not vanilla are not interned: equal to each other and to the custom item's type, not identical. Nothing is kept for identifiers Paletter does not know, so untrusted identifiers cannot grow memory: what is kept is bounded by the registered content. Equal custom items registered by different layers each own their type; those types are equal, not identical.

Referencing a type loads nothing. A vanilla constant the bundled data does not have (deprecated, or a preview item without the preview loaded) is not available and resolves to its fallback, normally minecraft:unknown.

Since:
0.1.0

      @Internal public static @NonNull BedrockItemType fromIdentifier(@NonNull String identifier)
      Plumbing: the type of an identifier: the vanilla constant if the identifier (after renames) is vanilla in the newest bundled data or has a generated constant, else a custom type known by its identifier only (not interned, so unknown identifiers never accumulate; equal, not identical, for equal identifiers). Loads the data. Use Palette.itemType(java.lang.String, org.geysermc.paletter.Lookup) or the constants of BedrockItems.

    • variant

      public @NonNull BedrockItemVariant variant(int damage)
      The variant of this type with a damage value, never null, and always of this type (also for a type that is not available: it resolves like any variant of it). The named constants of BedrockItemVariants and the variants the bundled data lists are the same instance every time, so == holds for them whenever the key was made. An aux nobody named gives a new variant without a canonical id (a layer can give it one with PaletteLayer.Builder.variant(ItemKey)); those are not kept, so arbitrary auxes cannot grow memory. Loads no bundled data: only the constants of BedrockItemVariants.
      Returns:
      the variant of this type with this aux value
